events.credibility_reason: Claimed full proof of a landmark problem (implies twin primes) with no review or uptake over ~25 years; later refereed work (Skorobogatov-Sofos, Inventiones 2023) treats H as open; venue is a Hadronic Press journal; the same paper claims finiteness/proofs for many other famous prime problems by one method.

Several F10 signals together: a resolution would imply twin primes and n^2+1 primes yet there is no uptake, citation or comment in ~17 months; Behajaina-Debes-Konig v2 (April 2026) still treats the integer case as open and only states a corollary conditional on H; single author at the margin of the field; venue (Preprints.org, not peer-reviewed) reviews nothing; the author claims H, Bateman-Horn and Chowla by the same method within seven months, and v1 of this DOI was titled as a note on Bateman-Horn (scope shift between versions).

Claims the stronger Bateman-Horn conjecture; same signals as the author's H preprint: no engagement, non-reviewing venue, same method claimed for H, BH and Chowla in rapid succession, later work treats the area as open.
Different problem (Chowla); same signals as the author's other claims: no engagement, non-reviewing venue, one method claimed to settle several famous conjectures.

why: The only post-snapshot claims to settle H are Xiao's Preprints.org papers. The H paper is scoped whole as claimed but judged not_credible: several F10 signals coincide (landmark consequences such as twin primes, no uptake in ~17 months, later 2026 work still treating the integer case as open, a venue that reviews nothing, one method claimed for H, Bateman-Horn and Chowla within months, and a title/scope change between v1 and v2). It is not judged on authorship or affiliation alone. Xiao's Bateman-Horn claim is a stronger form (variant) and Chowla is a different problem. Skorobogatov-Sofos's 100%-of-tuples density theorems are scored bound (a proportion), not case, because 'almost all tuples by height' does not settle any identifiable subclass of collections; both predate the snapshot. The polynomial-ring, PAC-field, number-field and namesake results are variants; the Bateman-Horn error-term and profinite papers bound or settle nothing about H. No AI system is credited in any event.
doubts: Xiao's texts were never opened (all 403), so the not_credible call rests on metadata and silence rather than an identified error; if a reader later confirms the argument this would flip. The Skorobogatov-Sofos density result could be read as case rather than bound; it predates the snapshot and neither tier yields open_stale, so the choice does not change the outcome. Jiang's 2001 paper was also unread.
